title: BTC to XMR Stuck in the Mempool: RBF, Fee Bumps, and What to Check

friendlyUrls.anchor: Bitcoin UTXOs, change outputs, and fees
whether a crypto transaction can be cancelled or reversed

keyQuestions: Why is my BTC to XMR swap still pending?
Should I send BTC again if my first deposit has zero confirmations?
Can I speed up BTC after sending it?
Can I use RBF for a BTC to XMR deposit?
Why did my TXID change after increasing the fee?
My BTC is confirmed. Why am I still waiting?
quickSteps: Find the BTC TXID and establish whether the deposit is unbroadcast, unconfirmed, or already confirmed.
Inspect the unconfirmed transaction before acting, including its fee conditions and any fee-bump controls offered by the sending wallet.
Verify the deposit output before approving an RBF replacement, and record both transaction IDs if the TXID changes.
Keep the Bitcoin transaction and the swap order as separate checkpoints; do not send another ordinary deposit just because one of them is still waiting.
Move the diagnosis downstream after confirmation: first to the order, then to the XMR payout and wallet if the swap has already completed.

issueRouting.start: The BTC to XMR order appears to be stuck or pending.

branches.if: There is no usable BTC TXID
then: Confirm whether the sending wallet actually created the Bitcoin transaction.
Check whether the wallet successfully broadcast the transaction.
Do not assume that a wallet error means a Bitcoin transaction exists.

branches.if: The BTC TXID exists but has zero confirmations
then: Inspect the transaction status and current fee conditions.
Check whether the sending wallet offers an appropriate RBF or fee-bump function.
Do not create a second ordinary BTC deposit as a shortcut.

branches.if: The BTC transaction is already confirmed
then: Stop treating the case as a Bitcoin mempool problem.
Compare the confirmed BTC payment with the current swap order status.
If the order is completed but XMR is not visible, move to XMR payout and wallet checks.

riskNotes: A pending Bitcoin transaction is not automatically a failed transaction.
Sending another ordinary BTC deposit can result in two separate payments if both transactions confirm.
Before approving an RBF replacement, verify that the intended BTC deposit output remains correct.
Keep the original and replacement TXIDs when a fee bump creates a new transaction ID.
Never provide a seed phrase or private key when requesting support for a delayed transaction.
